lens: Adversarial priority critic: P1 (disk writes must never drop frames, incl. frame-perfect cross-camera sync) and P3 (no unnecessary full-frame copies). Reviewed recommend_result.json against baseline_result.json, prototypes_result.json, cpp_result.json, verified_digest.json and the code at skellycam 23ccbf20 (git rev-parse HEAD = 23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d, so the checkout itself was read). One new functional test was run (writer crash safety, below); it is not a throughput benchmark.

issues.target: Plan as a whole (ranks 5 + 6, headline 'Make recording failure-isolated, counted and decoupled')
issues.problem: The plan does not guarantee P1; it converts silent loss into counted loss. The recorder's only buffer is the per-camera ring (1 GiB default = 172 slots = 2.87 s at 1080p BGR). Past that, the gated cursor either blocks the camera (sensor frames never grabbed, never on disk) or drops (frames never on disk). The plan states this itself ('A longer stall becomes counted loss, not silent loss', rank 6 risks) and lists spill-to-disk only as an open question. The ring cannot be sized 'from the measured worst stall' (rank 5 risks) because no real stall distribution was measured: P3 models a stall as a sleep, and no slow-disk, full-pSLC-cache (SN850X 91% full) or antivirus test was run.
issues.fix: Make 'no recorded frame is ever dropped' the design invariant, not a counter: (1) recording cursor policy = block only (never drop); (2) add an overflow tier that does not depend on the encoder or the disk keeping up, e.g. promote rank 7's compressed ring (about 154 s at 1080p by the plan's own arithmetic) or a RAM spill of JPEG-compressed frames, because raw BGR spill at 5x1080p60 is 1.87 GB/s (plan rank 8 arithmetic) and would hit the same disk; (3) measure worst-case writer stalls on this machine (Defender scan of a growing recording file, pSLC exhaustion at 91% fill, 10-minute 5x1080p60 run) and size RAM from that; (4) if the overflow tier is exhausted, stop the recording loudly with all cameras ending on the same frame number, instead of continuing with gaps.
issues.evidence: Ring size: ring_buffer_shared_memory.py L11 + L39-45 (memory_allocation=ONE_GIGABYTE // itemsize) https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/ipc/shared_memory/ring_buffer_shared_memory.py#L36-L52 . Block = sensor loss, drop = explicit loss: prototypes/results/p3_lossless_record.md part A, L=172 stall 3500 ms: block 180 sensor skipped, drop 190 ring-full drops (script prototypes/p3_lossless_record.py; stall is time.sleep at L105-107, 'all 5 at once' L14). Plan admits: recommend_result.json rank 6 risks_tradeoffs and open_questions[4]; prototypes_result.json limitations ('P3 models a stall as a sleep; no slow-disk / full pSLC-cache test was run. A spill-to-disk policy was not prototyped.').

issues.target: Recording container and shutdown path (rank 6 thread recorder, rank 13 NVENC MP4, WorkerRegistry.shutdown_all)
issues.problem: A process crash or forced terminate loses the whole MP4, not only the tail. HEAD's default writer is cv2 'X264' -> .mp4 and the plan keeps MP4 for the default MSMF path and for NVENC. In a new test, a writer process killed with Process.terminate() (TerminateProcess on Windows, no release()) left a 16.9 MB MP4 with 'moov atom not found' and 0 of 300 frames decodable; the same frames muxed as MJPEG-in-MKV and killed the same way decoded 298 of 300. The shutdown escalation gives workers only 3 s after the kill flag before terminate() (worker_registry.py L180-195). Today the inline recorder has no backlog, so the camera's finally block releases the file in time (opencv_camera_loop.py L124-127). Under rank 6, a recorder may hold up to 2.87 s of 1080p backlog (more after a disk stall, which is exactly when the backlog exists). Draining that before release can exceed the 3 s window, and then the entire recording file is lost. Rank 6 also prefers a thread inside the camera process to the separate process that P8 measured, so a camera-loop exception (L119-123: kill_everything then raise) takes the recorder down with it unless the thread is non-daemon and drains.
issues.fix: (1) Write crash-tolerant containers on every path: MKV, or fragmented MP4 via PyAV (movflags=frag_keyframe+empty_moov) for NVENC/libx264, or time-segmented files for MSMF. (2) Make shutdown drain-aware: the recorder reports its backlog, and shutdown_all waits for 'recorders drained and released' (bounded by backlog / measured encode rate plus margin) before terminate(). (3) Keep the recorder in its own process as P8 did, or specify a non-daemon thread that drains on camera-loop exit. (4) Add a fault-injection test: terminate a camera process mid-recording and assert that every frame up to the last committed one is decodable.

issues.target: Rank 1(d) (on kill flag: run stop_recording + finalize_recording with a timeout, then SIGTERM)
issues.problem: As written, rank 1(d) cannot work. Once global_kill_flag is set, ipc.should_continue is False (camera_group_ipc.py L47-53), so: every camera loop has already exited (opencv_camera_loop.py L43); stop_recording's pause awaits all_cameras_paused with no timeout (camera_group.py L218, camera_orchestrator.py L63-67), which never becomes true for exited loops; and finalize_recording's collection loop is guarded by ipc.should_continue (camera_group.py L328-334), so it exits at once and raises 'Not all cameras finished recording successfully' (L364-368). The per-frame timestamps exist only inside RecordingFinishedMessage (handle_recording_updates.py L50-57), so they are still lost. In addition, worker_registry SIGTERMs its own PID (L96, L107). On Windows that is TerminateProcess, so no atexit/shutdown_all runs in the main process.
issues.fix: Split the flag: one 'abort' flag that only stops capture after the recorders have drained, and one 'stop accepting new frames' state. Make data survival independent of finalize: move rank 6's incremental per-frame CSV write (and an fsync'd sidecar) into the S-effort first batch, so the timestamps are on disk whatever happens to the main process. Give pause/finalize explicit timeouts, and make finalize work from the on-disk CSVs.

issues.target: Headline / rank 6 / rank 12: frame-perfect sync vs the 59.95 fps result
issues.problem: The P2 headline (5x1080p 59.95 fps, 0 sensor frames lost) was measured with the lockstep grab gate removed and with recorders as separate processes. The recommended configuration (rank 6: recorder thread in the camera process, lockstep kept, frame_count set right after publish) was not measured. Rank 12 leaves 'keep lockstep at all?' open. Today frame-perfect sync rests on lockstep plus a per-camera software frame counter: frame_number increments once per successful retrieve (opencv_get_frame.py L79), each camera records [first, last) by that counter (camera_orchestrator.py L80-94), and lockstep keeps the counters within one grab of each other (L96-109). Without lockstep, every camera still records the same count, but frame N on camera A and frame N on camera B are no longer the same capture instant. Nothing in validation would detect it, because validate_recording only compares counts (recording_finalizer.py L168-170). So removing lockstep would trade sync, which is part of P1, for P2, and cross-camera timing spread was not measured.
issues.fix: State lockstep (or an equivalent group commit: a multiframe is recorded only when every camera has published that frame number) as a P1 requirement for recording. Re-run P8 with the gate kept and with the thread recorder actually proposed before claiming 59.95 fps for the plan. Do not adopt rank 12's gate removal without a measured timestamp-spread test.
issues.evidence: prototypes/p8_e2e_proto.py L8-9 ('No lockstep gate, no encode, no copy.copy') and L10 (recorder process); prototypes_result.json findings ('P8 removes SkellyCam's lockstep grab gate ... Cross-camera timing spread of free-running cameras was not measured'); recommend_result.json open_questions[1],[2]. issues.target: Rank 5 (3) 'explicit, counted policy: block or drop' for the recorder cursor
issues.problem: Allowing 'drop' on the recording cursor breaks equal per-camera frame counts whenever a stall hits one camera's writer and not the others: one antivirus scan of one file, one encoder session failure, one slow write. The recording then fails validate_recording (different frame counts raise ValueError) and loses frame-perfect sync. P3 tested only simultaneous stalls on all 5 recorders ('all 5 at once'), so the asymmetric case, which is the realistic one for P1, was never exercised. Without lockstep, 'block' on one camera also shifts that camera's frame numbers in time relative to the others.
issues.fix: For recording, allow block only, together with lockstep. Then a single camera's ring-full stalls the whole group equally, and the loss, if the overflow tier is exhausted, is the same frame numbers on every camera, counted by rank 4. Add a P3 variant with a stall on 1 of 5 recorders and assert identical recorded frame-number sets across cameras.
issues.evidence: prototypes/p3_lossless_record.py L14 ('ONE injected stall of S ms on every recorder at t=3 s (all 5 at once, like a disk stall)'); prototypes/proto_common.py L21-23 (block / drop / overwrite semantics); equal-count check https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/recorders/recording_finalizer.py#L147-L170

issues.target: Unaddressed drop path: stop_recording pauses capture while a recording is active
issues.problem: stop_recording pauses every camera (awaited) while first_recording_frame_number is still set and last_recording_frame_number is -1, i.e. while recording. Then it sets last = max(frame_count)+3 and unpauses. Paused loops only wait_1ms and never grab (opencv_camera_loop.py L63-65), so every recording has a silent sensor gap just before its last 3 frames. The gap lasts at least one await_10ms poll plus the pause/unpause handshakes. frame_number stays consecutive, so neither _validate_frame_number nor validate_recording can see it. No rank fixes this: rank 3(c) fixes only the start handshake, and rank 4 would at best count it.
issues.fix: Stop without pausing: publish last_recording_frame_number = max(frame_count) + margin while the cameras run (lockstep keeps the counts within one frame), and have each camera or recorder verify on arrival that it had not already passed it (the mirror of the rank-3(c) fix). Add a test that checks grab-timestamp intervals across the stop boundary.
issues.evidence: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera_group/camera_group.py#L215-L232 ; https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py#L60-L65 ; verified_digest.json write-path area, P1 risk 'Recording start and stop pause all cameras ... no frames are captured during the transition' (confirmed) and read-path area ('The same is true of the stop_recording pause'). Gap duration not measured: open question.

issues.problem: Rank 13 is labelled P2-only, but it reduces P1 margin and adds a failure mode with no handling. Its tick-to-written p99 is 218 ms (max 297 ms), which uses part of the 2.87 s ring budget. Sessions are capped at 12 per machine (the 13th open failed), and other applications (OBS, browsers, Discord) share that cap. The plan offers 'keep MSMF as fallback' only as a default choice. It says nothing about an encoder that fails to open at record start or fails mid-recording (driver reset or TDR). At HEAD, an exception in the recorder path goes through kill_everything (opencv_camera_loop.py L119-123); in rank 6's design the behaviour is unspecified, and the ring backlog of the failed camera would be lost.
issues.fix: Probe and reserve NVENC sessions before recording starts. If NVENC is unavailable, fall back for all cameras (to keep the format uniform). On a mid-recording encoder exception, keep the cursor where it is, reopen with the MSMF or MJPEG fallback into a new segment file, and continue from the same frame number. Count the event; never drop the backlog. Add an injection test (raise inside st.encode at frame k).
issues.evidence: prototypes/results/p5_nvenc.md session table (12 sessions, 13th ExternalError); prototypes/results/p8_e2e_summary.md p8_e2e_1080p_imdecode_nvenc.json (tick to written p99 218.2 ms, max 297.3 ms) as cited in recommend_result.json rank 13; https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py#L119-L123

issues.target: Rank 1 scope: other kill-flag paths still end every recording
issues.problem: Rank 1 removes the UI and FreeMoCap triggers, but any exception in any one camera loop still calls ipc.kill_everything() and ends all cameras' recordings (opencv_camera_loop.py L119-123). That includes rank 10's proposed 'raise if np.shares_memory is False', rank 2's CameraDisconnected, and rank 3's guards. A non-zero exit of any registered worker also sets the flag and SIGTERMs the server (worker_registry.py L86-97). Rank 1's own risk note ('keep escalation for camera-process errors but route it through a graceful stop') depends on the flag split, which the plan does not specify (see the rank 1(d) issue).
issues.fix: Define one graceful-stop path (drain recorders, write CSVs, release files, end all cameras on the same frame number) and route every camera-side error through it. Make rank 10's shares_memory mismatch fall back to one counted copy into the slot instead of raising.
issues.evidence: https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/camera/opencv/opencv_camera_loop.py#L119-L130 ; https://github.com/freemocap/skellycam/blob/23ccbf208e43879bfc74fc01049e5af2a623933d/skellycam/core/ipc/process_management/worker_registry.py#L83-L109 ; recommend_result.json rank 10 change ('raise if it is False') and rank 1 risks_tradeoffs.

issues.target: Rank 2 (skip put/record after 30 failed grabs, 'continue to the next gate check')
issues.problem: Skipping is correct for the frame counters: frame_number does not advance, and lockstep holds the other cameras, so counts stay equal. But the 'continue' option has no bound. A camera that keeps failing while still isOpened() holds the whole group at the lockstep gate indefinitely during a recording, and from then on every camera silently records nothing. Rank 4 would count this only after the fact.
issues.fix: Bound it: after a configurable time (for example 1 s) without a successful grab during recording, take the graceful stop. Expose failed_grabs live in the UI.

issues.target: Antivirus and GC stalls (named writer stalls the plan does not measure)
issues.problem: Windows Defender is known to touch this study's output files: it scanned P10's video files at the end of that run (background CPU up to 22.7%). The plan gives no Defender exclusion guidance for the recording folder or the recorder process, and no measured scan-induced write latency. GC pauses were not measured either. Rank 6's thread recorder shares a GIL and GC with the capture loop. Today video_frame_metadata grows by one recarray copy per frame (video_recorder.py L108), so gen-2 GC cost grows with recording length. Rank 6's incremental CSV removes that list, which helps.
issues.fix: Add a Defender-exclusion step to the install or diagnostics docs, and measure write() latency with and without real-time scanning during a 10-minute 5x1080p60 recording. Record gc.callbacks pause times in the recorder. Do the incremental CSV change early.

issues.problem: Rank 13 (NVENC) is listed as P2 only, but compared with MSMF fed a slot view it adds 2 full-size passes per frame: the BGR->I420 conversion and av.VideoFrame.from_ndarray, which copies the I420 buffer (1.5 B/px each). Rank 7 claims P3, but its consumer decode keeps a full-frame copy (np.copyto(slot, cv2.imdecode(...))) and adds a compressed-bytes copy into the JPEG ring. The plan's copy counts mention neither. None of these breaks P1, but they should be counted.
issues.fix: List these copies in ranks 7 and 13. For NVENC, try writing cvtColor output straight into a preallocated av.VideoFrame's planes (untested: open question). For rank 7, decode into the slot with a decoder that accepts a destination buffer (simplejpeg buffer=, bench venv only, P1: 4.68 vs 7.52 ms) or accept 1 copy per consumer-decoded frame and say so.
issues.evidence: prototypes/p8_e2e_proto.py L241-242 (cvtColor dst=i420 then from_ndarray), L369 copy note ('rec: I420 convert + from_ndarray copy (1.5 B/px each)'), L104 (np.copyto(v2, cv2.imdecode(...)) in the imdecode_off decoder thread), L171-173 (jring bytes copy); prototypes/p5_nvenc.py L17.

issues.target: Ranks with no P1 or P3 regression found (for balance)
issues.problem: No trade-off found in rank 8 (remove copy.copy; byte-identical slots), rank 3 (block config apply, reopen and the start race during recording), rank 1(a)-(c), or rank 14 (lapped views become counted skips in analysis, not on disk). Rank 9 (setNumThreads(1)) raises the inline record_frame median from 2.16 to 2.42 ms while the encode is still in the loop. That is a small P2 cost, and the result is provisional (P10). Rank 4 is detection only and prevents nothing.
issues.fix: Keep these. Ship rank 8 and rank 3 in the first batch. Do not count rank 4 as a P1 fix in the report.
issues.evidence: recommend_result.json ranks 1, 3, 4, 8, 9, 14; prototypes/results/p1_write.md (inplace_verified True x5); prototypes/results/p10_msmf_threads.md (PROVISIONAL).

open_questions: Distribution of real writer stalls on this machine (Defender real-time scan of growing MP4/MKV, pSLC exhaustion on the 91%-full SN850X, 10+ minute runs). Without it the ring cannot be sized for P1.
Length of the stop_recording pause gap in sensor frames (camera_group.py L215-232). Not measured.
Whether the MSMF sink writer ever drops frames internally under back-pressure, or always blocks write(). The baseline shows decoded == recorded at the tested rates only.
Whether a non-daemon recorder thread in the camera process is joined (and drains) when the camera loop raises, given multiprocessing child exit semantics. Not tested.
GC pause magnitude in the camera/recorder process during long recordings. Not measured.
Whether PyAV fragmented MP4 (movflags=frag_keyframe+empty_moov) with h264_nvenc survives terminate() the way MKV did. Not tested.
summary: The plan improves P1 a lot over HEAD (it removes the UI/FreeMoCap kill paths, guards config, start and reopen during recording, and adds a gated, counted recorder cursor), but it does not guarantee that disk writes never drop. (1) Beyond the 2.87 s ring (1080p, 1 GiB) a stall becomes counted loss, either as sensor skips (block) or as drops, and spill-to-disk and real stall measurements are missing. (2) A crash or a terminate() after shutdown_all's 3 s window loses the entire MP4: a new test killed an MSMF MP4 writer and left 0 of 300 frames decodable, while MJPEG-in-MKV kept 298 of 300. Rank 6's recorder backlog makes that window easier to miss. (3) Rank 1(d) cannot finalize after the kill flag is set, because the camera loops and finalize_recording both key on ipc.should_continue. (4) The stop_recording pause leaves an unaddressed silent gap in every recording. (5) Frame-perfect sync: the 59.95 fps headline was measured without lockstep, rank 12 leaves lockstep open, and rank 5 permits a 'drop' policy that yields unequal per-camera counts under the asymmetric stalls P3 never tested. Recording must use block plus lockstep (or a group commit). (6) The NVENC session-failure path is unhandled. On P3, no recommendation adds an unnecessary copy to the capture or recording hot path. Rank 8 and rank 10 remove copies, but ranks 7 and 13 carry uncounted conversion or decode copies.
